key_insight: Chain-of-thought reasoning can be made practical for edge devices by compressing verbose reasoning traces into compact, cache-friendly representations and distilling those compressed plans into small models — dramatically reducing token generation and KV-cache overhead without discarding the reasoning itself.
problem_solved: Makes LLM-style chain-of-thought reasoning feasible on resource-constrained edge hardware by addressing high token costs, large KV-cache footprints, and inefficient distillation of verbose reasoning traces into mobile models.
method: Compress verbose reasoning traces into compact latent or sketch representations that preserve reasoning steps but use far fewer tokens.
Adopt KV-cache–efficient inference (e.g., quantization, selective retrieval, or sparse storage) so cached reasoning state fits on-device with low memory and compute.
Distill reasoning into small student models via a two-stage teacher→compressed-plan→student pipeline where students learn to expand compact plans into full reasoning at inference time.
impact: Enables low-latency, low-memory chain-of-thought inference on phones and embedded devices, improving privacy, responsiveness, and energy efficiency for real-world mobile AI applications.
visual_elements: Before/After bar chart comparing token counts, KV-cache size, and latency (large LLM vs. compressed-edge pipeline).
Teacher→Compressor→Student diagram showing compressed plan passing from a large model to an on-device model.
Pipeline flowchart: generate reasoning → compress/store in KV-efficient format → expand at inference, annotated with memory/compute savings.
Icons representing edge device, chip/memory, compressed file, and a lightbulb (reasoning) to convey the concept at a glance.
paper_authors: Yelysei Bondarenko, Thomas Hehn, Rob Hesselink, Romain Lepert, Fabio Valerio Massoli
